Owner handbooks — searchable library

Search across all generations by job or keyword — try “oil”, “coolant”, “battery”, “torque”, “storage”. Tap any entry to read it right here.

📚 Every year, one tap — 1953 to today

Every single model year is listed below for everyone logged in — all there, nothing left out. Pick your exact year to open the full official book for it: 1984–today opens Chevrolet's free Manuals & Guides page — choose Corvette + your year for the official PDF. 1953–1982 opens the NCRS Owners Reference Library, the specialist source for the classic factory manuals. That full book is the final word for your exact year — tire pressure, wiper blades, fluids, fuses, torque, all of it.

Quick specs — the little stuff, not missed

The details owners actually hunt for. The exact number for your car is always in your year's manual (linked above) and, for tire pressure, on the driver's door-jamb placard — use these cards to find it fast and know what section to open.

🛞 Tire pressure (PSI)

Where it lives: Driver's door-jamb placard + “Tires & Wheels” in your year manual. Most modern Vettes (C5–C8) call for 30 PSI cold front & rear on factory sizes; classics vary by tire type — never use the max pressure printed on the tire sidewall. Check cold, monthly, and before any trip.

🌧️ Wiper blades

Where it lives: “Service & Maintenance / Wiper Blades” in your year manual, by exact year. Sizes change by generation — e.g. C5 uses 22″ both sides, C7 uses a longer driver blade than passenger — so confirm your year before buying, replace in pairs, and on C2/C3 check the vacuum wiper door too.

🛢️ Oil, coolant & fluids

Viscosity, Dexos spec (later cars), coolant type, brake fluid, and DCT / trans / diff intervals are all year-specific — open your year's book in the grid above, or search “oil” / “coolant” in the handbook search below. Classics on flat-tappet cams need zinc-appropriate oil.

🔩 Lug torque & jacking

Torque spec, star pattern, and factory jack points are in “Tires & Wheels / Vehicle Care” for your year. Re-check lug torque after ~50 miles on any wheel-off job. Fiberglass cars (C1–C3): lift only at factory points.

🔋 Battery & fuses

Battery group, location (it moves by generation — rear bins on many C5+ cars), fuse-box maps, and jump-start points are all diagrammed in your year manual under “Electrical”. Low voltage throws false codes on C5+ — test the battery first.

💡 Bulbs & headlights

Sealed beams (C1), vacuum pop-ups (C2/C3), gear-driven pop-ups (C4/C5), fixed lamps (C6+): bulb types and aiming live in “Lighting” for your year. See the Headlights handbook entry below for generation-by-generation fixes.

Full handbook for every generation — online & in print

The summaries below are quick reference. For the complete book for your exact year, use the link for your generation: newer cars get the free official PDF from Chevrolet; the classic generations go to the NCRS Owners Reference Library, which publishes the factory technical manuals & judging guides for 1953–82 cars.

📖 Want a physical, printed handbook?

Chevrolet's manuals page is also where you order a printed copy — GM's printing supplier is Helm, Inc. (the order link sits at the bottom of Chevrolet's Manuals & Guides page). GM's own manuals list Helm's order line as 1-800-551-4123, Mon–Fri 8am–6pm Eastern. Newer cars (2025–26) ship digital-only, so a printed book is an order, not a glovebox item. For C1–C3 paper books, the NCRS library above is the specialist source.
